title: How much milk is in each cup of tea?
description: One quarter of a litre of milk is shared among five cups. Dividing by five becomes multiplying by one fifth, and the two fractions multiply to give the milk in one cup. Keeko doubts the answer and thinks the milk should be multiplied by five.
teaching_notes: One idea: sharing a fraction equally among some cups is dividing by that number, which is multiplying by its reciprocal. Watch for students who multiply by five and get a share bigger than all the milk.

source: {{NAME_9}} made 5 cups of tea with 1/4 litre of milk. How much milk is there in each cup?
video_script.why: A learner sees a fraction shared among cups as a division, and the division as a multiplication by a reciprocal.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question of five cups of tea and one quarter of a litre of milk
video_script.anchor: five cups of tea and the one quarter litre of milk that {{NAME_9}} used
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the milk by the number of cups, which gives a share bigger than all the milk
video_script.payoff_line: Each cup has one twentieth of a litre of milk.
video_script.fraction_reading: one quarter, one fifth, one twentieth, five quarters

names.{{NAME_9}}: the person who makes five cups of tea with one quarter of a litre of milk

maths_rules: the slip: 5 x 1/4 = 5/4, which is more than 1/4
video_script.design: Five cups in a row and one quarter litre of milk; the working band builds the division, the reciprocal and the product line by line.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; five cups in a row and the words one quarter litre of milk

marks.milk: the quarter litre label lights up over the cups
marks.ask: a question mark appears over one cup

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about {{NAME_9}} and five cups of tea.
<bookmark mark='milk'/>{{NAME_9}} used one quarter of a litre of milk for all the cups together.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much milk is there in each cup of tea?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits beside the cups

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the quarter litre split among five cups; then 1/5 written beside the 5

marks.share: the milk spreads equally over the five cups
marks.recip: 1/5 is written beside 5 and joined to it

narration: <bookmark mark='share'/>Picture the milk shared equally among the five cups.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Sharing equally among five means dividing by five.
<bookmark mark='recip'/>The fraction one over five is called the reciprocal of five.
Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1/4 litre of milk in 5 cups
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one quarter of a litre of milk is used in five cups of tea.

marks.find: the words milk in one cup are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the milk in one cup.

beats.on_screen: 5 × (milk per cup) = 1/4, so milk per cup = 1/4 ÷ 5

marks.times: the line five times milk per cup equals one quarter is written
marks.divide: the division one quarter divided by five is written

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step one, five times the milk in one cup is one quarter.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>The milk in one cup is one quarter divided by five, because the milk is shared.

marks.recip: one fifth is written as the reciprocal of five
marks.swap: the division sign turns into a multiplication sign

narration: <bookmark mark='recip'/>Step two, the reciprocal of the divisor five is one fifth.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>We multiply the dividend, one quarter, by this reciprocal, one fifth, as in the method of your book.

marks.top: the numerators one and one are joined by a times sign
marks.bottom: the denominators four and five are joined by a times sign

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step three, multiply the numerators, one times one.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>Then multiply the denominators, four times five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Each cup has one twentieth of a litre of milk.
Five cups of one twentieth make back the one quarter we started with.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the five cups
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 5 × 1/4 = 5/4 crossed out; the cups are shown with the one quarter litre as a small part of the milk

marks.big: 5/4 is shown bigger than the one quarter litre
marks.fix: 5/4 is crossed out and the division by five returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each cup gets five quarters of a litre, after multiplying the milk by five.
<bookmark mark='big'/>But five quarters of a litre is more than all the milk {{NAME_9}} had.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Sharing among cups makes each share smaller, so we divide by five.
